newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir allies win Sarawak polls but see upsets.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir allies win Sarawak polls but see upsets.

text.p: A coalition of four parties linked to Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad was returned to power in Sarawak state elections as widely expected on Sunday, but suffered setbacks when it lost five seats.

Local television stations reported that, as of 1500 GMT, the coalition which is a part of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's National Front party had won 57 of a total of 62 seats in the Sarawak state assembly. The Sarawak National Front had won 19 seats uncontested on nomination day at the end of August.
But the coalition lost five seats, including the defeat of the state's Deputy Chief Minister Wong Soon Kai.
Wong lost to a candidate from Malaysia's main opposition party, the Democratic Action Party (DAP). The DAP also won two other seats, the first time it has been voted into the state assembly.
Two seats were taken by independent candidates, a rare feat in a Sarawak state election.

Sarawak National Front leaders said the defeats were a setback, as it had controlled all 56 seats in the previous government in the timber and oil-rich state located on Borneo island. Six new seats were added in the just-concluded elections.
Mahathir said over a private television channel that he was baffled why Sarawakians had voted in the DAP, the National Front's main opposition in the federal parliament.
He said the voters may have felt they had nothing to lose, as the Sarawak National Front had been widely expected to win.
"There was a feeling among voters that results of the elections were a foregone conclusion. They were not worried that there might be a change of government," he said over a TV3 news broadcast.
Sarawak -- about as large as peninsular Malaysia itself -- is one of the poorest and least developed states in Malaysia, despite being rich in resources.
The state's 1.7 million population comprises a dozen or so tribes, with the biggest represented in the governing coalition by their own parties.
Malaysia is the world's largest exporter of tropical timber and Sarawak accounts for nearly 80 percent of this.

Belaga, the state constituency in which the controversial $5.5 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam project is being built, was won by the National Front. The project, which had angered environmentalists as it would flood an area the size of Singapore in the lush rainforests, was not a major issue in the elections.
